title: Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: MOT electric vehicle transition efforts
sections.summary: MOT is working in three areas, and this Bill covers the third: updating regulations for EV chargers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) is undertaking efforts in three areas to enable this transition: first, reviewing the EV tax structure; second, developing the charging network and infrastructure; and third, reviewing the regulatory regime for EV chargers and EV charging services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This Bill has to do with the third prong of our efforts: update and strengthen the regulations for chargers that serve EVs, which include electric cars, motorcycles, goods vehicles and buses.

sections.label: LTA regulating EVs and chargers
sections.summary: LTA, as vehicle licensing authority, will regulate both EVs and EV chargers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA, as the vehicle licensing authority, will be the agency to regulate both EVs and EV chargers.

sections.label: LTA setting EV charger standards
sections.summary: The Bill gives LTA the function of setting technical standards for all EV chargers in Singapore for public safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Third, the Bill charges LTA with the function of setting technical standards for all EV chargers in Singapore in the interest of public safety.

sections.label: Safety concerns for motorists and residents
sections.summary: Safety concerns arise for motorists and building occupiers and residents because most charging stations would be at housing estates and commercial buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, safety concerns for both motorists and building occupiers and residents, given that most of the charging stations going forward would be located at housing estates and commercial buildings.

sections.label: Tender allocation and agency coordination
sections.summary: Questions ask how LTA will allocate charging point tenders and EV types, and how HDB, Town Councils and EMA will work together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As technology on the batteries develops, how will LTA allocate the tenders for charging points and types of EV vehicles over the next five to 10 years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With increased deployment of EV charging points in the housing estates, how will agencies like HDB, Town Councils and EMA work together for installation, maintenance and safety issues?

sections.label: US energy department electrification study
sections.summary: A US energy department study found increased electrification across all sectors could boost national consumption by as much as 38% by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: An energy department study done in the context of the US found that increased electrification across all sectors of the economy could boost national consumption by as much as 38% by 2050.

sections.label: EV charging points tender bidders
sections.summary: A public tender for EV charging points at about 200 public carparks drew 19 bidders, covering over 600 points for 12 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: On 1 April 2021, it was reported in The Straits Times that a public tender for the installation of EV charging points at some 200 public carparks across Singapore has drawn 19 bidders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The tender called for bidders to build, operate and maintain more than 600 charging points for 12 years, starting as early as 31 August this year.

sections.label: MCST charger lease approval
sections.summary: An MCST may still need 75% to 90% resident resolution for a charger lease despite companies footing upfront installation fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Mr Ong Ye Kung replied that there are certain places, such as SP Mobility, Greenlots and Charge+, who are willing to foot the upfront installation fees for EV charges in return for collecting charging revenue for a period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: One of the condominium MCSTs in my constituency has already provided feedback that, given the conditions of the lease of chargers, with one of the companies mentioned by the Minister, they may still need to obtain between 75% and 90% general or special resolution approval from residents for the lease anyway.

sections.label: ICE versus EV emissions study
sections.summary: Borneo Motors CEO shared an internal study showing ICE vehicles emit 50% and 25% more carbon dioxide than EVs and hybrid EVs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Borneo Motors CEO, Jasmmine Wong, shared with me the results of a study they have done internally which shows that Internal Combustion Engine, or ICE, vehicles emit 50% and 25% more carbon dioxide than EVs and hybrid EVs respectively.

sections.label: 60,000 EV charging points by 2030
sections.summary: The Minister for Transport announced that by 2030 there are plans for 60,000 EV charging points across the island.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During the Committee of Supply, the Minister for Transport announced that, by 2030, it is planned that there will be 60,000 EV charging points available across the island.

sections.label: EV lots in CSFS GFA exemptions
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Government will consider including EV lots in URA's Community/Sports Facilities Scheme, which allows GFA exemptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To help accelerate provision of fast-charging stations, will the Government consider EV lots to be included in URA's existing Community/Sports Facilities Scheme, or CSFS, which allows Gross Floor Area, or GFA, exemptions?

sections.label: Re-skilling workshop mechanics and technicians
sections.summary: The second broad theme concerns re-skilling the mechanics and technicians in the workshops.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second broad theme is around re-skilling the mechanics and technicians in the workshops.

sections.label: Hybrid COE category review
sections.summary: Hybrids cut carbon dioxide emissions by 25% versus ICE vehicles, and the industry suggests LTA review COE Category classification for hybrids.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hybrid's carbon dioxide emission reduction of 25%, compared to an ICE, is considerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To encourage hybrid adoption alongside EV adoption, the industry has a suggestion for LTA to review the COE Category classification for hybrid vehicles.

sections.label: Used car emission penalties
sections.summary: The passage asks what regulatory changes apply to used cars and whether C1 and C2 banding penalties apply at COE renewal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we pursue the transition to cleaner energy vehicles, with the various policies for new vehicle registration, what regulatory changes will the Government be making with regard to used cars?

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the same penalty policies for C1 and C2 banding guidelines for new cars be applied for used cars, if their emission test results at point of COE renewal fail to meet the mark?

sections.label: Battery prices driven down
sections.summary: Global government and private investment has driven battery prices to as low as $130 per kilowatt hour, averaging about $180.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thanks to market forces, with investment from governments and people across the world, battery prices have been driven down to as low as $130 per kilowatt hour today, with the average at about $180.

sections.label: EV incentives and road tax
sections.summary: From January 2022 to December 2023 the minimum ARF of $5,000 is lowered to zero for EVs, which pay no fuel excise duties, and EV owners pay an additional $700 road tax from 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As per the latest EV incentives announced in Budget 2021, from January 2022 to December 2023, the minimum ARF of $5,000 will be lowered to zero dollars for all EVs – and EVs do not pay fuel excise duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given this, EV owners will be made to pay an additional $700 road tax from 2023 with a phase-in period from 2021.

sections.label: EV e-waste and EPR scheme
sections.summary: EVs produce considerable e-waste from higher battery and semiconductor content, and the e-waste Extended Producer Responsibility scheme starts 1 July 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: EVs produce considerable e-waste with the higher battery and semiconductor content and the EPR or Extended Producer Responsibility scheme for e-waste will be in place from 1 July 2021.

sections.label: EV battery recycling and legislation
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there are targets to increase EV battery recycling and material recovery and whether Government will legislate end-of-life battery management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, promoting e-waste recovery from batteries could be a competence we could nurture in Singapore so that Singapore-based companies can invest in the region to export this know-how.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask if there are targets to increase EV battery recycling and material recovery and is the Government looking to legislate the end-of-life management of EV batteries to mandate reuse and material recovery rather than disposal?

sections.label: Public transport mode share target
sections.summary: The Land Transport Master Plan 2040 aimed to raise peak hour public transport mode share to 75%, and it appears to have crossed 67% recently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of the key goals in the Land Transport Master Plan 2040 announced in 2019 was to increase the peak hour public transport mode share to 75%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We are on track to meet this target as we appear to have crossed 67% very recently.

sections.label: Publishing consultation findings
sections.summary: A Member asks if the Government will publish more consultation findings, noting only 39% of 126 REACH consultations had full findings published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Government also commit to publishing more of its consultations unless there are specific business sensitivity reasons not to do so?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note that in the reply to one of my recent Parliamentary Questions, only 39% of 126 consultations published on REACH over the past five years had their findings or summary of responses published in full.

sections.label: Transport electrification targets
sections.summary: The Ministry has set targets to stop diesel car registration, roll out EV-ready towns, and have 60,000 charging points by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the area of transport, the Ministry has set ambitious targets to cease registration of diesel cars and roll out EV-ready towns, with a target of 60,000 charging points nationwide by 2030.

sections.label: EV charging point distribution
sections.summary: A Deloitte report found over 70% of charging was at residential locations, and the Government plans 60% of 60,000 points in public carparks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A Deloitte report on EV public charging infrastructure highlighted that more than 70% of charging took place at residential locations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is heartening to know that the Government has planned for 60% of the 60,000 charging points to be in public carparks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On average, 15% of the existing carpark lots will be converted to overnight charging points.

sections.label: EV charging accessibility in Bill
sections.summary: The Member notes the Bill does not direct LTA to keep public EV charging points widely accessible or affordable, or ensure market competition.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For this to be achieved, new low emissions mobility options must be widely available to all.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note that there is no provision in the Bill that directs LTA to ensure that charging points for EVs in public areas, including HDB estates and public vehicle parking facilities, remain widely accessible.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Bill also does not prescribe the role of LTA to ensure that charging points are made available in a manner that is affordable to the public, including ensuring sufficient competition in the market to encourage fair pricing for consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The convenience and benefits of owning an EV must not only be reserved for residents who live in landed properties as they can easily purchase, install and access their own charging points in their own properties.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note that the RFI being conducted by LTA right now does consider deploying 60,000 charging points by 2030, including 40,000 points in public and HDB carparks.

sections.label: EV waste and COE duration
sections.summary: The Member says consideration is needed for managing electronic waste from expired EVs and whether the 10-year COE duration remains relevant.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moving on from equity to sustainability, we should also ensure that there is sufficient consideration for how we would manage inevitable growth in electronic waste from expired EVs and whether the 10-year duration for COEs remains relevant, given the potentially low emissions beyond the 10-year life of the electric car.

sections.label: Dedicated bike lanes and Sengkang
sections.summary: The speaker cites cycling's lower emissions and calls for the Government to let Sengkang lead in embracing a cycling culture.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Having dedicated bike lanes on roads and pop-up bicycle lanes that are separate from both pedestrians and motor vehicles are good ways to encourage alternative means of transport, not just for leisure but also for commuting.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is especially important when you consider that cycling was estimated to emit 10 times less emissions than electric cars by a recent study.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In fact, the study also found that the average person who shifted from car to bike for just one week, one day a week, cut their carbon footprint by 3.2 kilos of carbon dioxide, equivalent to the emissions from driving a car for 10 kilometres, eating a serving of red meat or chocolate or sending 800 emails.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With this in mind, I would like to call for the Government to allow Sengkang to lead the charge in becoming one of the first towns to fully embrace a cycling culture, with a dense network of cycling paths and pedestrian-friendly infrastructure.

sections.label: Green Mark and end-of-trip facilities
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether on-site end-of-trip features like showers and changing rooms could eventually be made mandatory for new and renovated office spaces.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I note that BCA's Green Mark gives a point for buildings that provide sheltered bicycle lots, adequate facilities like showers and changing rooms, can we go a step further to eventually make such on-site end-of-trip features mandatory for new and renovated office spaces?

sections.label: Tokyo and Taiwan petrol motorcycle bans
sections.summary: Tokyo and Taiwan have both announced that they would ban sales of petrol motorcycles by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Tokyo and Taiwan have both announced that they would ban sales of petrol motorcycles by 2035.

sections.label: Electric versus petrol motorcycle registrations
sections.summary: By the end of the year, one electric motorcycle was registered compared to 140,000 petrol motorcycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By the end of the year, a grand total of one electric motorcycle was registered, compared to 140,000 petrol motorcycles.

sections.label: Condominium households in 2020
sections.summary: Sixteen percent of households live in condominiums, based on 2020 data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Sixteen percent of our households live in condominiums, based on 2020 data.

sections.label: Ontario condominium EV charging rule
sections.summary: Ontario introduced a regulation requiring condominium associations to install EV charging points when a resident makes a reasonable request.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Ontario, Canada’s largest province, introduced a regulation requiring condominium associations to install EV charging points as long as a resident makes a reasonable request.

sections.label: Vehicles and carbon emissions
sections.summary: Vehicles contribute 50% of carbon emissions, and the industry seeks more fuel-efficient cars and reduced greenhouse emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that vehicles contribute to 50% of carbon emissions, this industry has been continuously looking for ways to make cars more fuel-efficient while also reducing greenhouse emissions.

sections.label: Electric propulsion as way forward
sections.summary: In the past five to eight years, the industry has chosen electric propulsion as a credible replacement for internal combustion engines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the past five to eight years, the industry has landed on electric propulsion as the way forward and it is a very credible replacement for internal combustion engines.

sections.label: Heavy vehicle accidents and motorcyclist fatalities
sections.summary: In Singapore, accidents involving heavy vehicles remain high and motorcyclist fatalities continue to exceed 50 a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In Singapore, as it is, accidents involving heavy vehicles continue to be high and the number of motorcyclist fatalities continue to be more than 50 a year.

sections.label: Modified Tesla Model 3 performance
sections.summary: A modified Tesla Model 3 can cut two seconds off its zero to 100 kilometres per hour pace, with modifications available online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, a modified Tesla Model 3 can shave off two seconds of its zero to 100 kilometres per hour pace through modifications and all of this is available on the Internet.

sections.label: Charging stations per vehicle target
sections.summary: With 980,000 vehicles, the target of 60,000 charging stations by 2030 means one charging station for every 16.3 vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Based on our population of 980,000 vehicles, our target of 60,000 charging stations by 2030 will mean that there is one charging station for every 16.3 vehicles.

sections.label: Lessons from BlueSG chargers
sections.summary: With 1,800 charging stations already and BlueSG a main EV rental player, the question asks what lessons can be learned from BlueSG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As there are already 1,800 charging stations and BlueSG is one of the main players for rental of EVs, what lessons can we learn from BlueSG with its current fleet of vehicles and 1,800 chargers?

sections.label: Pre-1990s housing electrical load upgrade
sections.summary: Houses built before the 1990s need their 30-amp switch upgraded to 40-amp, and the question asks whether ELU has factored in increased electrical load from charging stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Houses built before the 1990s need to have their 30-amp switch upgraded to a 40-amp switch, and has ELU now factored in the increased electrical load brought about by the charging stations in our estates?

sections.label: Goal of fully electric vehicle population
sections.summary: Achieving an entirely EV population by 2040 requires significant change in vehicle management while ensuring infrastructure is adequate to accommodate these vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our goal of achieving an entirely EV population by 2040 requires a significant change in the way we manage vehicles, while ensuring that our infrastructure is adequate to accommodate these vehicles.

sections.label: Drivers' charging infrastructure concerns
sections.summary: With 40,000 active drivers in 2020 driving around 300 kilometres a day, drivers seek assurance that charging capabilities will withstand the complete shift to electric.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With 40,000 reported active drivers in 2020 and with drivers driving around 300 kilometres a day, our drivers seek assurance that charging capabilities will stand the test of the P2P driving industry with the complete shift to electric.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Any lapses in charging infrastructure – be it unexpected charging station breakdowns or the unavailability of charging stations – can compromise an entire shift or even an entire day's work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As it is, there is a lack of clarity with the availability of fast-charging points and the economic balance of having vehicles rested in a typical eight-hour charging cycle.

sections.label: Government coordination on EV policies
sections.summary: Considerations must be watched with drivers' livelihoods as priority, and Government must work with taxi companies and ride hailing platforms on EV policy implications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These considerations must be tightly watched and implemented with the interest of our drivers' livelihoods as a priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is imperative then for our Government to work closely with taxi companies and ride hailing platforms to work out the implications of policies and infrastructure that accompany the electric push in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we are honest with ourselves, Singapore is a little slow on the mark with EVs – with adoption rates around 0.2% versus more than 10% in cities like London and Berlin and only some 2,000-plus EV chargers in the market.

sections.label: Bill gives LTA EV mandate
sections.summary: The amendments proposed in the Bill give LTA a clear mandate to drive promotion and regulation of EVs and development of EV charging infrastructure and standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The amendments proposed in the Bill gives LTA the clear mandate to drive the promotion and regulation of EVs and the development of EV charging infrastructure as well as standards.

sections.label: Question on plug-in hybrids, hydrogen
sections.summary: As the EV space is still evolving, the question asks whether this includes plug-in hybrids as well as hydrogen-fuelled vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As the EV space is still evolving, I would like to ask if this includes plug-in hybrids as well as hydrogen-fuelled vehicles.

sections.label: Ministry plans for end-of-life batteries
sections.summary: The passage asks what the Ministry's plans are for these batteries at the end of their life cycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's plans for these batteries at the end of their life cycles?

sections.label: EV charging and generating units
sections.summary: The Minister for Transport said switching light vehicles to EVs with most owners charging around the same time may require adding one or two new 600-megawatt generating units, around 8% to 16% of current peak demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The Minister for Transport earlier mentioned that if our light vehicles switch to EVs and most EV owners charge around the same time of the day, we may need to add one or two new 600-megawatt electricity generating units in our power generation system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: This amounts to around 8% to 16% of the current overall peak electricity demand in Singapore.

sections.label: Grid stability and charging points
sections.summary: This will keep the electricity grid stable as substations are unlikely to exceed capacity due to EV charging, and 40,000 charging points are planned at public carparks by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: This will ensure that the electricity grid remains stable, as substations are unlikely to exceed capacity due to EV charging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We have announced our plan to roll out 40,000 charging points at our public carparks by 2030.

sections.label: Charging points at private premises
sections.summary: The target is 20,000 charging points deployed at private premises by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Indeed, we target 20,000 charging points to be deployed at private premises by 2030.

sections.label: EPR scheme for EV batteries
sections.summary: From July this year, NEA will implement an Extended Producer Responsibility scheme making EV battery producers responsible for proper treatment at end-of-life, with an appointed operator collecting consumer EV batteries for licensed e-waste recyclers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: From July this year, the National Environment Agency, or NEA, will implement an Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) scheme to ensure the proper treatment and recycling of regulated electrical and electronic waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Under the scheme, producers of EV batteries are responsible for the proper treatment of the batteries when they reach end-of-life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: NEA has also appointed an operator to collect consumer EV batteries on behalf of the producers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: All collected EV batteries are to be sent for proper treatment with licensed e-waste recyclers.
